AbstractText.Label: AIM
AbstractText.content: The purpose of this qualitative research was to explore perspectives of administrators (n = 581) regarding advantages and challenges of employing part-time nurse faculty (PTNF) in schools of nursing in the United States.

AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: The nursing faculty shortage has resulted in increased reliance on PTNF who are clinical experts but often inexperienced as educators. A broader evidence base is necessary to develop effective strategies to support and retain these faculty members.

AbstractText.Label: METHOD
AbstractText.content: Deans and directors of schools of nursing were invited to complete an online survey with two open-ended questions about the use of PTNF.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Five themes emerged from the qualitative descriptive analysis: clinical practice as primary role, diversity of educational approaches, effects on full-time faculty role, economic impact, and contracted educator role. Both positive and negative aspects of each theme were identified.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: Results of this study support specific efforts to provide professional development and support to PTNF.

Article.ArticleTitle: Administrator Perspectives of Advantages and Challenges of Employing Part-Time Faculty in Nursing Education Programs: Two Sides of the Same Coin.
